teaser.text: Public Storage sells the right to use space, not the things stored in it. A dollar comes in mainly as monthly rent, pays the costs of keeping that space ready, and then passes through the other costs of owning and operating a real-estate company.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Public Storage?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires weak housing turnover and local competition to keep replacement rents below departing-tenant rents. Promotions rise, same-store NOI stays weak, and higher refinancing costs limit the acquired portfolios’ contribution. Investors then apply a lower multiple while the dividend remains covered but less flexible. The price falls to $231.21 at the first date and $210.68 at the last. Its probability is 28%, above the individual driver odds because operating weakness and integration risk can reinforce each other.

The bull case requires stronger housing activity, moderating supply, effective rent growth without excessive move-outs, successful NSA integration, and faster development lease-up. The price reaches $318.66 initially and $395.13 finally. Its probability is 18% because the operating record is weak and the synergy target is not yet earned income.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Public Storage really make?

paragraphs.text: PSA paid $2.11 billion in dividends in 2025. It spent $218.8 million on maintenance capital expenditures in 2025 and $310.7 million on development and expansion. Replacing roofs, gates and paving consumes cash even when an earnings measure adjusts for that spending, so the gap between Core FFO and dividends supports debt repayment, acquisitions, development or liquidity rather than guaranteeing surplus cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Public Storage today?

paragraphs.text: The base multiple is 16.5x in every forecast year. The bear case compresses from 14.0x to 13.0x, while the bull case expands from 18.0x to 20.0x. Today’s price is about 17.6x trailing Core FFO, so the base case assumes confidence stabilizes without a growth premium.

blocks.heading: How much does Public Storage pay in dividends over time?

paragraphs.text: Total NOI rose through 2025, but same-store NOI fell in both 2024 and 2025. Occupancy slipped in 2025, move-in contract rent remained below move-out rent, leverage rose, fixed-charge coverage edged down, and Core FFO per share recovered in 2025 to above 2023. The dividend stayed at $12.00 per share in 2024 and 2025, with coverage competing with upkeep and investment.

blocks.heading: What could change Public Storage's dividend?

paragraphs.subsection: 5.8 — Capital structure, debt cost and dividend capacity
paragraphs.text: A specialist therefore stress-tests the dividend against lower rent growth, higher property costs, maintenance needs and refinancing costs. The accounts support a dividend with room, but they do not show unlimited surplus cash. PSA’s central challenge is to turn improving occupancy and new-customer prices into durable same-store NOI before debt and capital demands take more of the cash flow.

The dividend stays at $12.00 per share in the first year, then rises to $12.60 in the base case. Coverage supports restraint rather than aggressive growth: 2025 Core FFO per share was $16.97 against a $12.00 dividend. The bear case cuts the payout to $11.00 as financing pressure persists; the bull case reaches $13.23 through stronger AFFO growth.

blocks.heading: What is Public Storage's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: The dividend supplies current income, while the share price also reflects hopes for better rents and property earnings. That yield was below the 10-year Treasury yield of 5.09% observed on October 16, 2026, so the stock’s appeal depends partly on growth and on the value investors place on owning property.

blocks.heading: Has Public Storage kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, the cash incentive weighted Core FFO growth at 60%; strategic management goals carried 30%, with the remainder tied to net asset value growth. Public Storage reported Core FFO growth of 1.8% and NAV growth of 2.2%, both in line with budget, so those components paid at target.

blocks.heading: What is Public Storage's last eight-quarter trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue increased from the comparable quarter, while NOI was nearly flat. FFO per share rose sharply, but Core FFO per share declined. The difference was largely currency: PSA recorded a $17.2 million foreign-currency gain in Q2 2026 after a $146.1 million loss in Q2 2025. That comparison says more about euro debt than about the stores.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Public Storage's next results?

paragraphs.text: The earnings release is scheduled for October 26, and the call for October 27. The central test is whether new properties and acquisitions are starting to offset weaker mature facilities without pushing borrowing and dilution beyond what future income can support.
